title: Pearl Material: Nacre Science
text_faithful: The faith view states that each gate was of one pearl (Revelation 21:21, short excerpt). The material view describes what pearl actually is, so that the claim and the material are never confused: pearl is nacre, not a single engineered substance.
engineering: Nacre, or mother-of-pearl, is a composite of thin aragonite (calcium carbonate) tablets, about 0.5 micrometres thick, glued by organic biopolymer layers about 20 to 30 nanometres thick. The brick-and-mortar structure gives nacre both iridescence and remarkable toughness for a ceramic-like material.
body:
History and description: Pearls form in molluscs around an irritant, layer by layer, and natural pearls large enough for jewellery are already rare; a gate-sized natural pearl does not occur. Cultured pearls, grown with an implanted nucleus, dominate the modern market and are genuine nacre over a nucleus, not solid nacre through.

Science proof: Science proof: nacre's fracture toughness (about 3 to 9 MPa square-root-metre in published measurements, versus about 1 for monolithic aragonite) comes from crack deflection at tablet interfaces and tablet sliding. Its iridescence comes from thin-film interference across the stacked tablets, a measurable optical effect.

Mathematics and computation: Computation: the demo estimates the number of aragonite tablets in a 1 mm nacre layer and the Bragg reflection wavelength for a tablet-plus-polymer period, the core nacre optics calculation.

Demonstration program: the demo program below computes the numbers in the mathematics section when executed; its exact output is stored as expected_output.

Status label: established. Faith and engineering views are kept distinct in this record; nothing speculative is presented as established, and nothing established is presented as speculative.

Both routes exist at laboratory and specialty-product scale; neither produces gate-sized solid nacre.

title: Gate Dimensions and Tolerances
text_faithful: The faith view gives no gate dimensions; Revelation 21 gives wall and city measures, not gate leaf sizes. All dimensions in this record are therefore design assumptions, labelled as such, not textual claims.
engineering: A design gate leaf of 3 metres wide by 4 metres tall, in two leaves, with a 50 mm structural frame tolerance zone, is a reasonable human-scale assumption for a monumental entrance. Tolerances govern whether leaves meet, seals compress evenly, and hinges carry load without binding.
body:
History and description: Tolerance analysis (stack-up) is standard engineering: each part contributes its variation, and the assembly gap is the sum of the parts' variations in the worst case, or the root-sum-square in the statistical case. Designing to the worst case is conservative; designing to the statistical case requires process control evidence.

Science proof: Science proof, as engineering method: the demo computes both worst-case and statistical stack-ups for four interface dimensions, showing that the statistical gap is smaller but depends on an assumption of independent, controlled variation.

Mathematics and computation: Computation: worst-case sums absolute tolerances; statistical takes the square root of the sum of squares; both are reported so the choice is visible.

engineering: Circulation design asks how many people can pass a gate per hour, how queues form, and how districts connect without bottlenecks. A gate's throughput is its width times a flow rate per metre, minus a factor for security checks, groups, and accessibility needs.

Mathematics and computation: Computation: throughput equals width times flow rate times 60 minutes; excess arrivals become queue length.

title: Gate Safety and Egress
text_faithful: The faith view describes open gates; safety engineering describes how people leave quickly in an emergency, which is a separate requirement that applies whether gates are normally open or closed.
engineering: Egress design is governed by established life-safety practice: sufficient exit width, clear routes, emergency lighting, signage, and drills. The governing arithmetic is that required egress time must be less than available safe time, with a margin, for the largest expected crowd.
body:
History and description: Egress failures in history have come from locked exits, narrow passages, and crowd pressure at bottlenecks, which is why modern codes require exits to open in the direction of escape and to remain unobstructed. A monumental gate that cannot be opened outward under crowd pressure is a hazard, not a feature.

Science proof: Science proof: the demo computes egress time for a crowd through a gate of given width at a conservative flow, and compares it with a 180-second available-time assumption, reporting the margin.

Mathematics and computation: Computation: egress time equals crowd divided by (width times flow per minute), converted to seconds.

Demonstration program: the demo program below computes the numbers in the mathematics section when executed; its exact output is stored as expected_output.

title: Gate Manufacturing Yield
text_faithful: The faith view does not discuss manufacturing yield. Yield is the fraction of started panels that pass inspection, and it governs how many must be started to finish a gate, a basic production-planning fact.
engineering: Yield multiplies across steps: if coating yields 90 percent and assembly yields 95 percent, the combined yield is 85.5 percent, not the average of the two. Low-yield steps dominate, which is why yield improvement targets the worst step first.

title: Gate Joining and Sealing
text_faithful: The faith view describes gates as single pearls; the joining record addresses the buildable target, nacre-inspired panels, which must be joined and sealed, unlike a single stone.
engineering: Panel joints need a structural connection (mechanical fasteners or bonded joints), a movement allowance for thermal expansion, and a weather seal (gaskets or sealants) that keeps water out while allowing movement. A joint that is rigid in all directions will crack when temperatures change.
body:
History and description: Thermal movement is predictable: a panel's length change equals its expansion coefficient times its length times its temperature change. Sealants are chosen by movement capability, the percentage of joint-width change they can absorb without failure.

title: Gate Deviation Register
text_faithful: The faith view describes an ideal gate; the deviation register records where a real gate differs from its design, and why. It is a quality document, not a confession of failure: every built structure deviates, and the register is what makes deviations manageable.
engineering: Each register entry records the deviation, its measured size, its cause, its effect on function and safety, and its disposition: use as-is, repair, or replace. A deviation without a disposition is an open item, and an open safety deviation blocks acceptance.

History and description: Deviation registers are established practice in construction, aerospace, and manufacturing, where they are called nonconformance reports. The discipline is the same: measure, record, decide, and close, with the decision signed, not assumed.

safety_open = sum(1 for _, s, saf in REG if s == 'open' and saf)
